sounds.intro: Romanian is written in the Latin alphabet and is a Romance language, so many words look like Italian or Spanish. It is spelled almost exactly as it sounds. Nouns are masculine, feminine or neuter. The stress is usually on the second-to-last syllable.
rows: a short, flat "uh", like the "a" in "about"
a deep, throaty "uh", said far back in the mouth
notes: "c" before e or i is "ch", and "g" before e or i is "j". To get a hard "c" or "g" before e or i, Romanian writes "ch" or "gh".
"i" at the end of a word is often almost silent. It softens the consonant before it: lupi (lups).

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Romanian often drops the pronoun, because the verb ending shows who is speaking. "El" is he, "ea" is she. "Tu" is informal and "dumneavoastră" is very formal.
ex: ea este sora mea mai mare
yah YES-teh SOH-rah myah my MAH-reh

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: The plural endings change the last letters: -e, -i, -uri. carte, cărți. casă, case. copil, copii.

grammar.title: To be: a fi
text: "A fi" (to be) is irregular. Learn all the forms. The pronoun is usually dropped.

grammar.title: A avea: have
text: "A avea" (to have): am, ai, are, avem, aveți, au.

grammar.title: Present tense
text: The ending shows the person. A lucra (to work): lucrez, lucrezi, lucrează, lucrăm, lucrați, lucrează.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The usual order is who, verb, what, but Romanian is flexible. The article goes after the noun: carte (a book), cartea (the book).

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put "nu" before the verb: merg (I go), nu merg (I do not go).
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: The word order does not change. Just raise your voice at the end. You can also start with "oare" for a softer question.

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stand at the start of the sentence.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: The word comes after the noun and agrees with it: cartea mea (my book), cartea ta (your book), cartea lui (his), cartea ei (her), cartea noastră (our), cartea voastră (your, formal), cartea lor (their). To like something, say "îmi place".

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: tu (informal): friends, family, children. dumneavoastră / voi (formal): strangers, older people, work. The verb changes: -i (informal), -ți (formal).
rows: ce mai faci? / ce mai faceți?
cheh my fahch / cheh my fah-CHETS

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: "am" + the participle: am mers (I went). Future: "voi" + the basic verb, or "o să": voi merge, o să merg.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: the short form (vino). Formal and plural: add -ți (veniți). To forbid, put "nu" in front: nu veni.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: A putea (can): pot să. A trebui (must): trebuie să. A vrea (want): vreau să. The second verb is in the "să" form.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Common words: în (in), pe (on), la (at, to), de la (from), cu (with), sub (under), lângă (next to).
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Put "mai" before the adjective for "more": mai mare. For "the most" use "cel mai": cel mai mare. "Than" is "decât".
rows: mare, mai mare, cel mai mare
mic, mai mic, cel mai mic
